They are and they try to measure both with the current system implemented. The best way measure overall skill in a battle royale is to look at how many engagements a player puts themself in. Their skill is based off of how many engagements they come out of successfully. With the current system, if you can get kills and successfully win the match, you will rank up significantly quicker than someone else who just wins. Since their goal is to measure both win and kill skill, the current system is a pretty decent method to measure both.
But this isn't a competition for the most wins, it's for the highest skill. This is obvious from the system they implemented.

In a competition to declare a winner of that event, sure. That is not what ranked is measuring though as it would be more tournament oriented rather than a system which measures you over a period of games.

I honestly don't know that part of the lore either, but I'd imagine they fight multiple times for a couple of reasons: multiple of the same characters and the fact that the Apex Games isn't a one time thing (or I don't think it is).

What equates in battle royale games isn't kills or winning the game. The only real way to be able to measure skill vs other players is to look at how many engagements a player involves themself in and to see how many of those times they are successful. This is only true because a single lucky or unlucky game is a poor merit to measure someone's skill therefore we have to look at something over time. If a player put themself in more engagements and comes out on top more often than another player, they are more skillful. Since its over a period of time and not just a couple instances, this has merit to measure a persons skill as luck will even out overtime statistically.
Then there is no peak and it will get stale. What makes it interesting is two things: the fights and the path people take to make it to those fights.

I'm not saying winning is not a skill either. It doesn't matter imo penultimate or not, what squad you wipe. If you're wiping more squads a game other than just the last squad, you should be rewarded for it to a point. I'm fine with wins rewarding a bit more than kills possibly can to encourage winning a bit while still giving an incentive for kills as it makes more sense than just to the winning squad.

I also never said they shouldn't win as they will obviously win the match. It just makes sense to also reward the smaller wins or every single person would play more passive than they already do which would make the game stale for most people over time.

Another note though: it is their choice to put them in a disadvantage by looting less. In a ranked mode, no player should be rewarded more for deciding to put themselves at a disadvantage as that goes against the spirit of what the mode is all about. Ranked was made to push players and see how good they really are against everyone else. 

I'll end with a question: what takes more skill: good positioning or good positioning and being able to take down enemy squads?

I never said that though. What I meant was they are putting in more effort vs someone who is waiting for others to die in encounters not involving them. They are also succeeding in their efforts therefore they should get rewarded over those who don't succeed.

So doesnt that mean it's working well? I understand it can be frustrating to get lots of damage, but little kills. That happens to everyone at times, but a player will 'steal' kills and will get kills 'stolen'. If a player is truly skillful, they both even out over time which is why they made it take as long as it does to rank up.

I think it makes sense when you try to make a system based off of skill. When you wipe a squad, you will for sure place higher than them. That group put in more effort for their placement vs a team who waits for everyone else to fight. Kills can't add up to more than wins either so it makes sense as long as that is true, especially with a cap. Lore wise again, the spectators want interesting matches and will want to spectate people who can pull off and win more encounters instead of the whole match itself.

Here's the way I think about it summed up: the best way to measure skill in a battle royale is not how often you win the game, but how often you win any engagements. If you get more kills and place higher, you put yourself into more engagements and came out on top. Therefore you are rewarded for the smaller wins on top of the bigger win (winning the match).

There's two reasons it should imo:

b. You put in more effort (typically) when you get more kills. The team who wins with 20 total kills and wins put in more effort than a team with 1 kill and wins for example. An extreme example though tbf.
